Ev
ery command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it c
ontacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries cre
dentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error mas
ks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own serve
r: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` u
ses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid`
/ `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and
successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--

quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

oud commands pick one project:

# Local Evals

> Run a

n MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcomin
g SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads
disabled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavio
r.\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a m
odel, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring yo
ur own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing
.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the
run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.
md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.\n\n## Eval identity and loc
al data\n\nRun `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `api
Key` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the s
aved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an o
rganization admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transien
t failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI reso
lves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organizat
ion.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API
headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surf
ace (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom exe
cutors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server
URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned itera
tions are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`,
`MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain loca

l unless result uploading is enabled separately.

## Quick start

### 1. Write a suite

Save this as `.mcpjam/evals/example.

yaml`:

```yaml theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
schemaVersion: "2"
mode: agentWorkflow
reportingMode: standard
suite:\

n id: s_notes_example
 name: Notes server
target:
 servers:
 - name: notes
defaults:
 judge:
 enabled: false
 m

odel: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
 iterations: 1
 passThreshold: 1
 validity: {}
cases:
 - id: c_reads_a_note
 title:

reads the note it was asked about
 steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: What does note 7 say?

- id: a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 type: toolCalledAtLeastOnce
 toolName: read_note
 - id:

c_never_deletes
 title: never deletes when only asked to read
 steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 promp

t: Summarize note 7.
 - id: a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 type: toolNeverCalled
 toolNam

e: delete_note
```

`mcpjam cloud eval validate --file .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml` checks the file offline, with no account.
\
n### 2. Configure the server\n\n`mcpjam test` binds each `target.servers[].name` to a local MCP config. The simplest is a `.mcp.js
\"command\": \"node\",\n \"args\": [\"./notes-server.js\"],\n \"env\": { \"NOTES_DB\": \"${NOTES_DB:-./notes.db}\"

ACTED]
mcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml
```

### 4. Fail one on purpose, then rerun it

Change `toolName: read_note` t
o `toolName: echo` in the first case and run again: the command exits `1` and names the failing assertion. Fix it, then rerun just

s_a_note --reporter junit-xml --out reports/local.xml
```

`--case` takes the exact authored id and is repeatable.

## Server

bindings

For each target server name, the first source with an entry wins — the whole entry, never a field-level merge:

1.
`--server <name>=<url>` (repeatable; HTTP(S) only). For a suite with exactly one target, `--url` / `--command` and their auth flag
s bind it instead.\n2. `--mcp-config <path>` — an explicit MCP JSON config. A missing or invalid explicit file fails setup.\n3. `.

/.mcp.json`
4. `./.mcpjam/mcp.json`

Paths are relative to the directory you run the command in, not to the suite file. An expl
icit `--mcp-config` can bind some servers while the two conventional files still supply the rest. A lower-precedence file is read
only while names remain unbound, and entries for servers the suite does not target are ignored — their processes are never started
. Every name still unbound is reported together (exit `4`).\n\nConfig entries use the standard `mcpServers` shape (`command`/`args
`/`env`/`cwd` for stdio, `url`/`headers` for HTTP, with `type`/`transport` spellings such as `stdio`, `http`, `sse`, `streamable-h
ttp`). `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` are expanded in the winning entries only; an unset `${VAR}` fails setup naming the variable,
